chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abu al-Bakhtari, raising it (to the Imam), said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The believers are calm and lenient, like the nosed camel; when it is tied, it submits, and if it is knelt down upon a rock, it kneels down.'

key_terms.الْجَمَلِ الْأَنِفِ: The nosed camel (a camel with a ring in its nose, indicating it is trained and obedient)

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of a true believer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith characterizes the believer as possessing a gentle and pliable nature, using the metaphor of a well-trained camel that submits readily to its handler, even when kneeling on rough terrain, to illustrate spiritual humility and patience. This imagery reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of *infiyad* (yielding) not as weakness, but as a disciplined ease in accepting divine will and enduring worldly trials with grace. The comparison highlights the believer's adaptability and lack of stubbornness in the face of life's hardships.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Abu Al Bakhtary, raising it, said,
‘I heard himasws saying: ‘The Momineen are calm and lenient like the nosed camel when it is towed it goes (wherever guided to), and if it is knelt down upon a rock, it kneels down’.
en.sarwar: 14. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from abu al-Bakhtari in a marfu’ manner from the Imam who has said the following:
‘‘Believers are of serenity and soft words. They are easy to lead like the camel harnessed by the nose, who does not resist the leader who makes him sit even on a rock.”
